note: The five classes an engineering tool can belong to, and the fixed order in which a transport is resolved. Data, not logic. scripts/tools.py reads this; adding a class or a transport kind is done here plus, only if the kind needs runtime probing, one helper in tools.py.

AGENT_HOST.summary: An IDE or agent runtime the skills run inside. Not a provider the framework resolves — it is where resolution happens. Listed for completeness and kept out of `tools status`.
AGENT_HOST.resolved_by: host registration (lib/hosts.registry), not the engineering tool resolver

LOCAL_TOOL.summary: A program the agent runs in a shell on this machine. No network identity of its own; auth, when needed, is the local daemon's or the user's ambient login.

REMOTE_SERVICE.summary: A hosted service reached over the network. Needs an identity: an already-authenticated CLI or host MCP server first, a stored credential only as a last resort.

RUNTIME_RESOURCE.summary: A live system whose current state is the evidence — a cluster, a broker. Reached through a client that already holds a context/config; reads are bounded because the state is large and moving.

DATA_RESOURCE.summary: A datastore. Schema and bounded read-only queries are in scope; administration is not. Connects through a native client and a named connection profile.

resolution_order.summary: A capability the agent host already exposes as a first-class tool. Nothing to install or authenticate.
An MCP server the host already has configured. Zero marginal context cost; never ask the operator to add one mid-task.
An already-authenticated official CLI (gh, glab, aws, gcloud, az, kubectl, jira, ...). It holds its own credential, so the agent never handles a secret.
A local/native tool or protocol client on PATH (docker, terraform, psql, kafka tooling, npm, mvn).
A named connection profile resolved through the Access Resolver — used for data resources and internal services with no CLI/MCP.
A direct API adapter, configured through the Access Resolver. The fallback, never the first choice.
Nothing above worked. Report the missing capability and safe setup guidance. Never invent a credential prompt.
